terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; what one gloats over in the ablative, or in + abl.
evidence: Cic. Balb. 58: in ruīnīs alicujus exsultāre (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Rosc. Am. 16: victōriā exsultāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “leap up”: to exult, with the cause in the ablative (laetitiā, gaudiō); over another’s misfortune, in ruīnīs alicujus.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 321.
